description: This topic examines how to recognise healthy and sick animals, the causes and common types of livestock diseases in Tanzania, internal and external parasites, and the methods of disease prevention and control including the role of the veterinary officer.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a sign that shows an animal is healthy?
mcq.explanation: A healthy animal has a smooth, shiny coat, bright eyes and a good appetite, while a sick animal often looks dull and isolated.

mcq.questionText: Diseases caused by tiny organisms that can only be seen using a microscope and that often reproduce inside body cells are caused by:
mcq.explanation: Viruses are extremely small disease-causing agents that multiply inside the cells of the host animal.

mcq.questionText: East Coast Fever, a serious cattle disease in Tanzania, is transmitted mainly by:
mcq.explanation: East Coast Fever is a protozoan disease of cattle spread by ticks, which is why regular dipping helps to control it.

mcq.questionText: Newcastle disease is a viral disease that mostly affects which type of livestock?
mcq.explanation: Newcastle disease is a highly contagious viral disease of poultry that can kill many birds and is controlled by vaccination.

mcq.questionText: Which method is used to control external parasites such as ticks on cattle?
mcq.explanation: Dipping or spraying cattle with acaricides kills ticks and other external parasites on the skin.

mcq.questionText: Foot-and-mouth disease is best described as a disease that is:

options.text: Caused by ticks and not contagious
Highly contagious and caused by a virus

mcq.explanation: Foot-and-mouth disease is a highly contagious viral disease causing blisters in the mouth and on the feet of cloven-hoofed animals.

mcq.questionText: Roundworms and tapeworms that live inside the stomach and intestines of animals are examples of:
mcq.explanation: Internal parasites such as roundworms and tapeworms live inside the body of the host and are controlled by deworming.

mcq.questionText: The practice of giving animals a vaccine in order to protect them against a particular disease is called:
mcq.explanation: Vaccination introduces a vaccine that makes the animal develop immunity against a specific disease before it is exposed to it.

mcq.questionText: Anthrax is a dangerous livestock disease in Tanzania that is caused by:
mcq.explanation: Anthrax is caused by a spore-forming bacterium and can affect both animals and humans, so infected carcasses must not be opened.

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following is an external parasite of livestock?
mcq.explanation: Ticks live on the outside of the animal's body and feed on blood, making them external parasites.

mcq.questionText: Keeping animal houses clean, dry and well ventilated is an example of disease control through:
mcq.explanation: Cleanliness and proper sanitation reduce the build-up of germs and parasites, helping to prevent disease.

mcq.questionText: A trained professional who diagnoses, treats and advises farmers on animal diseases is known as a:
mcq.explanation: A veterinary officer is trained in animal health and provides diagnosis, treatment, vaccination and advice to livestock keepers.

mcq.questionText: Why is it important to separate a newly bought or sick animal from the rest of the herd?

options.text: To prevent the spread of disease to healthy animals

mcq.explanation: Isolation or quarantine of new or sick animals stops infections from passing to the rest of the herd.

mcq.questionText: Heavy infestation of an animal with internal parasites such as worms is most likely to cause:

options.text: A shiny coat and weight gain
Loss of weight, weakness and poor growth

mcq.explanation: Worms feed on the animal's nutrients and blood, leading to weight loss, weakness, anaemia and stunted growth.

mcq.questionText: A farmer notices several cattle with sudden high fever, swollen lymph nodes near the ears, and many ticks on their bodies. The MOST likely disease and control measure are:

options.text: East Coast Fever, controlled by regular dipping against ticks
Foot-and-mouth disease, controlled by spraying houses

mcq.explanation: Fever, swollen lymph nodes and the presence of ticks point to East Coast Fever, which is controlled by tick control through dipping or spraying.

fib.questionText: An animal that has bright eyes, a good appetite and a shiny coat is described as being _____.
fib.explanation: These observable signs are used to identify a healthy animal.

fib.questionText: Parasites that live on the outside of an animal's body, such as ticks and lice, are called _____ parasites.
fib.explanation: External parasites live on the skin and outer surface of the host.

fib.questionText: Worms and flukes that live inside the body of an animal are known as _____ parasites.
fib.explanation: Internal parasites live inside organs such as the stomach, intestines and liver.

fib.questionText: The process of dipping cattle in a tank containing acaricide is mainly done to control _____.
fib.explanation: Dipping kills ticks and other external parasites on the animal's skin.

fib.questionText: A substance given to an animal to make it develop immunity against a particular disease is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A vaccine stimulates the animal's body to build protection against a specific disease.

fib.questionText: East Coast Fever in cattle is caused by a microscopic organism belonging to the group called _____.
fib.explanation: Protozoa are single-celled organisms; the protozoan causing ECF is transmitted by ticks.

fib.questionText: Anthrax and many other livestock diseases are caused by single-celled organisms called _____.
fib.explanation: Bacteria are micro-organisms that cause diseases such as anthrax.

fib.questionText: The giving of drugs to an animal to kill internal parasites such as roundworms is called _____.
fib.explanation: Deworming, also called drenching, removes worms from the animal's digestive system.

fib.questionText: Separating new or sick animals from the rest of the herd to prevent disease spread is called _____.
fib.explanation: Quarantine isolates animals that may be carrying a disease until they are confirmed healthy.

fib.questionText: The trained animal health expert who treats sick animals and advises farmers is called a veterinary _____.
fib.explanation: A veterinary officer offers diagnosis, treatment, vaccination and advice on animal health.

tf.questionText: A sick animal usually shows a poor appetite, dull eyes and a rough coat.
tf.explanation: These are common signs that an animal is unwell.

tf.questionText: Newcastle disease mainly affects cattle and is caused by ticks.
tf.explanation: Newcastle disease is a viral disease that mainly affects poultry, not cattle, and is not spread by ticks.

tf.questionText: Ticks are external parasites that feed on the blood of livestock.
tf.explanation: Ticks attach to the skin and suck blood, and can also transmit diseases such as East Coast Fever.

tf.questionText: Foot-and-mouth disease is a highly contagious disease that spreads quickly from one animal to another.
tf.explanation: Foot-and-mouth disease spreads rapidly among cloven-hoofed animals, which is why movement control is important.

tf.questionText: Vaccination is used to treat an animal that is already seriously sick with a disease.
tf.explanation: Vaccination is a preventive measure given before infection to build immunity, not a cure for an already sick animal.

tf.questionText: Keeping animal houses dirty and overcrowded helps to reduce the spread of diseases.
tf.explanation: Dirty and overcrowded conditions increase germs and parasites and therefore promote the spread of diseases.

tf.questionText: Anthrax can affect both animals and human beings.
tf.explanation: Anthrax is a zoonotic bacterial disease that can pass from animals to humans.

tf.questionText: Roundworms and tapeworms are examples of internal parasites of livestock.
tf.explanation: Both live inside the digestive system of the animal and are controlled by deworming.

tf.questionText: A veterinary officer can advise farmers on how to prevent and control animal diseases.
tf.explanation: Advising farmers on prevention, control, treatment and vaccination is a key role of the veterinary officer.

tf.questionText: Regular dipping of cattle has no effect on the spread of tick-borne diseases.
tf.explanation: Dipping controls ticks and therefore reduces the spread of tick-borne diseases such as East Coast Fever.

summary.correctAnswer: Bright eyes, good appetite, shiny coat, alertness and normal movement.
summary.explanation: These visible signs help a farmer judge that an animal is in good health.

summary.correctAnswer: Dull eyes, loss of appetite, rough coat, isolation and weakness.
summary.explanation: Recognising these signs early allows quick treatment and prevents disease spread.
Different disease-causing agents lead to different livestock diseases.

summary.correctAnswer: Parasites living inside the body, such as roundworms, tapeworms and liver flukes.
summary.explanation: They are controlled by deworming and good hygiene.

summary.correctAnswer: Parasites living on the body surface, such as ticks, lice, mites and fleas.
summary.explanation: They are controlled by dipping or spraying with acaricides.

summary.correctAnswer: A protozoan disease of cattle spread by ticks, causing fever and swollen lymph nodes.
summary.explanation: It is controlled by tick control through regular dipping.

summary.correctAnswer: A highly contagious viral disease of poultry controlled by vaccination.
summary.explanation: It can cause heavy bird losses if birds are not vaccinated.

summary.correctAnswer: A highly contagious viral disease causing blisters in the mouth and on the feet.
summary.explanation: It is controlled by movement restriction, quarantine and vaccination.

summary.questionText: Methods of disease prevention and control
summary.correctAnswer: Vaccination, dipping, deworming, good hygiene, proper feeding and quarantine.
summary.explanation: Combining these methods keeps livestock healthy and productive.

summary.correctAnswer: Diagnoses, treats and vaccinates animals and advises farmers on disease control.
summary.explanation: The veterinary officer is the key professional in maintaining livestock health.

hoq.questionText: A farmer vaccinates poultry against Newcastle disease but still keeps the flock in dirty, overcrowded houses and mixes new birds with the old ones without quarantine. Why might disease outbreaks still occur?

options.text: Vaccination alone removes the need for all other control measures
Poor hygiene and lack of quarantine still allow other diseases and infections to spread
Vaccines make birds more likely to fall sick
Overcrowding improves the immunity of the birds

hoq.explanation: A vaccine only protects against the specific disease vaccinated for; dirty, crowded conditions and unquarantined new birds still allow other diseases and parasites to spread.

hoq.questionText: Two neighbouring farmers keep cattle. One dips his animals regularly while the other never does. Over time, which farmer is MORE likely to suffer losses from East Coast Fever and why?

options.text: The one who dips, because dipping spreads ticks
The one who never dips, because uncontrolled ticks transmit the disease
Neither, because East Coast Fever is not linked to ticks
Both equally, because dipping has no effect on ticks

hoq.explanation: East Coast Fever is spread by ticks, so the farmer who never dips has uncontrolled ticks and is more likely to lose cattle to the disease.

hoq.questionText: An animal that is regularly dewormed and well fed still becomes weak, loses weight and has many ticks on its body. Which combined explanation BEST fits this situation?

options.text: Deworming should have killed the ticks, so the diagnosis must be wrong
Deworming controls internal worms only, while the ticks (external parasites) are still draining blood and may transmit disease
Good feeding always prevents every type of parasite
Ticks cannot affect an animal that has been dewormed

hoq.explanation: Deworming only removes internal parasites; ticks are external parasites that still suck blood and can transmit tick-borne diseases, so separate tick control such as dipping is needed.
